## Introduction

This document walks through a complete scripted workflow for
[SWAT-MODFLOW](https://swat.tamu.edu/software/swat-modflow/) that mirrors
the **QSWATMOD2** QGIS plugin tabs, but runs entirely in Python — no QGIS
installation required.

The workflow uses **Scenario C** (build MODFLOW from scratch) to create a
fully working example in `data/qswatmod-test/` from the QSWAT model data in
`data/swat/`.  The resulting folder structure mirrors what the QGIS plugin
produces in `data/SWAT-MODFLOW/`.

The workflow is implemented in the `swatmf` package bundled with this
repository.  Install it (once) from the project root:

```bash
pip install -e .
```

The sections below follow the same tabs as the QSWATMOD2 plugin:

| # | Section | Plugin tab |
|---|---------|-----------|
| 1 | Setup — paths and simulation period | *(common)* |
| 2 | **Pre-Processing** — SWAT inputs, MODFLOW options, river connections, linking, RT3D | Pre-Processing |
| 3 | **Simulation** — pumping, drain cells, groundwater delay | Simulation |
| 4 | Streamflow | Post-Processing |
| 5 | Groundwater Levels | Post-Processing |
| 6 | MODFLOW Recharge | Post-Processing |
| 7 | GW–SW Exchange | Post-Processing |
| 8 | Water Balance | Post-Processing |
| 9 | **RT3D** — Reactive Transport (NO₃, P) | Post-Processing |
| 10 | Performance Metrics Summary | *(summary)* |

---

## 1  Setup

### 1.1  Project paths

The example data bundled with this repository lives under `data/`.  The QGIS plugin (QSWATMOD2) creates a standard project folder that contains
all of the data needed for the coupled model.  The layout it produces is:

| Variable | Points to | Contains |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| `project_dir` / `wd` | Project root (= SWAT TxtInOut) | `file.cio`, `*.hru`, `*.gw`, `output.*` … |
| `org_shps` | `GIS/org_shps/` | `hru_org.shp`, `sub_org.shp`, `riv_org.shp`, `mf_grid.gpkg`, MODFLOW rasters |
| `sm_shps` | `GIS/SMshps/` | `hru_link.gpkg`, `sub_link.gpkg`, `dhru_grid_link.gpkg`, `river_grid.shp` … |
| `table_dir` | `GIS/Table/` | `hru_dhru`, `dhru_grid`, `river_grid`, `swatmf_link.txt` |
| `exe_dir` | `SM_exes/` | `SWAT-MODFLOW3.exe`, `swatmf_rel*.exe`, `CreateSWATMF.exe` |
| `run_dir` | `SWAT-MODFLOW/` | Coupled run folder — SWAT files + MODFLOW files assembled here |
| `mf_wd` | MODFLOW model folder | `.dis`, `.bas`, `.nam`, `.nwt`, `.upw`, `.riv`, `.oc` … |

`mf_wd` is the folder that holds the MODFLOW input files.  In many projects
the MODFLOW files are placed directly in `run_dir` (the coupled run folder)
or kept in a separate user-supplied directory.

```{python}
import os
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ── PROJ conflict fix ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# TauDEM ships an older PROJ database that can shadow rasterio's bundled one.
# Force PROJ_DATA to rasterio's own proj_data directory before any imports
# that touch PROJ (rasterio, geopandas, pyproj …).
import rasterio as _rasterio
os.environ["PROJ_DATA"] = os.path.join(
    os.path.dirname(_rasterio.__file__), "proj_data"
)
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

REPO_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath("workflow.qmd"))

# ── Source data (QSWAT project) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Root of the QSWAT project that contains the SWAT TxtInOut and shapefiles.
swat_project = os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "data", "swat")

# SWAT TxtInOut folder inside the QSWAT project.
swat_txtinout = os.path.join(swat_project, "Scenarios", "Default", "TxtInOut")

# SWAT watershed shapefiles (HRU, subbasin, river).
swat_shapes = os.path.join(swat_project, "Watershed", "Shapes")

# DEM raster — used by Scenario C to build the MODFLOW model from scratch.
dem_path = os.path.join(swat_project, "Source", "dem.tif")

# ── Target project folder (qswatmod-test) ───────────────────────────────────
# This is the QSWATMOD2-style project folder that this workflow will create.
project_dir = os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "data", "qswatmod-test")

# SWAT TxtInOut = the project root (SWAT files are copied here in Section 1.3).
wd = project_dir

# GIS subfolder structure (mirrors the QGIS plugin layout).
gis_dir   = os.path.join(project_dir, "GIS")
org_shps  = os.path.join(gis_dir, "org_shps")   # original shapefiles, MODFLOW rasters, mf_grid.gpkg
sm_shps   = os.path.join(gis_dir, "SMshps")      # linkage shapefiles
table_dir = os.path.join(gis_dir, "Table")       # link tables + swatmf_link.txt

# Executables folder.
exe_dir = os.path.join(project_dir, "SM_exes")

# Coupled run folder — SWAT + MODFLOW files assembled here for the simulation.
run_dir = os.path.join(project_dir, "SWAT-MODFLOW")

# mf_wd will be set to the MODFLOW folder in Section 2.2 (Scenario C).
# For Scenarios A/B it would point to an existing model folder.
mf_wd = run_dir   # placeholder — overwritten in Scenario C

# Output folder for exported results.
out = os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "outputs")
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

print("SWAT source TxtInOut  :", swat_txtinout)
print("Project folder        :", project_dir)
print("GIS / org_shps        :", org_shps)
print("GIS / Table           :", table_dir)
print("Coupled run folder    :", run_dir)
```

### 1.2  Project Setup

Create the QSWATMOD2-style folder structure in `data/qswatmod-test/` and
populate it with the SWAT TxtInOut files and shapefiles from `data/swat/`.
This step is only needed once — it is safe to re-run (files are overwritten).

```{python}
import shutil, glob

# ── Create folder structure ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
for folder in [project_dir, gis_dir, org_shps, sm_shps, table_dir,
               exe_dir, run_dir,
               os.path.join(run_dir, "GIS", "org_shps"),
               os.path.join(run_dir, "GIS", "SMshps"),
               os.path.join(run_dir, "GIS", "Table"),
               os.path.join(project_dir, "Scenarios"),
               os.path.join(project_dir, "DB"),
               os.path.join(project_dir, "exported_files")]:
    os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)

print("Folder structure created.")
```

```{python}
# ── Copy SWAT TxtInOut files to the project root ────────────────────────────
# The QGIS plugin places all SWAT files at the project root level.
swat_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(swat_txtinout, "*"))
n_copied = 0
for src in swat_files:
    dst = os.path.join(project_dir, os.path.basename(src))
    _ = shutil.copy2(src, dst)
    n_copied += 1

print(f"Copied {n_copied} SWAT TxtInOut files → {project_dir}")
```

```{python}
# ── Copy SWAT TxtInOut files to the coupled run folder too ──────────────────
# run_dir needs an identical copy — it is the folder the executable runs from.
n_run = 0
for src in swat_files:
    dst = os.path.join(run_dir, os.path.basename(src))
    _ = shutil.copy2(src, dst)
    n_run += 1

print(f"Copied {n_run} SWAT TxtInOut files → {run_dir}")
```

```{python}
# ── Copy SWAT shapefiles to org_shps (rename to plugin naming convention) ───
shp_map = {
    "hru1": "hru_org",    # HRU polygons   → hru_org.shp
    "subs1": "sub_org",   # Subbasin polys → sub_org.shp
    "riv1": "riv_org",    # River lines    → riv_org.shp
}
extensions = [".shp", ".dbf", ".shx", ".prj", ".cpg"]

for src_stem, dst_stem in shp_map.items():
    for ext in extensions:
        src = os.path.join(swat_shapes, src_stem + ext)
        dst = os.path.join(org_shps,   dst_stem + ext)
        if os.path.isfile(src):
            _ = shutil.copy2(src, dst)

print("Shapefiles copied to org_shps:")
for src_stem, dst_stem in shp_map.items():
    print(f"  {src_stem}.shp  →  {dst_stem}.shp")
```

```{python}
# ── Copy executables from the reference project ──────────────────────────────
# Source: data/SWAT-MODFLOW/SM_exes/ (ships with the repository)
ref_exe_dir = os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "data", "SWAT-MODFLOW", "SM_exes")

exe_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(ref_exe_dir, "*.exe"))
for exe in exe_files:
    _ = shutil.copy2(exe, os.path.join(exe_dir, os.path.basename(exe)))
    print(f"  {os.path.basename(exe)}")

print("Executables copied to SM_exes/")
```

### 1.3  Simulation period

The simulation dates are read from `file.cio`.

The example model runs **9 years (1980 – 1988)** with a 1-year warm-up, so
output starts from 1981.  SWAT is configured for **daily** output
(`IPRINT = 1`).

```{python}
from swatmf import parse_file_cio

sp = parse_file_cio(wd)

print(f"Simulation start  : {sp.start_date.date()}")
print(f"Simulation end    : {sp.end_date.date()}")
print(f"Warm-up start     : {sp.start_date_warmup.date()}")
print(f"Warm-up end       : {sp.end_date_warmup.date()}")
print(f"Warm-up years     : {sp.skipyear}")
print(f"SWAT iprint code  : {sp.iprint}  "
      f"({'daily' if sp.iprint==1 else 'monthly' if sp.iprint==0 else 'annual'})")
```

```{python}
# Convenience date strings used throughout
start_str  = sp.start_date_warmup.strftime("%m/%d/%Y")    # for pandas date_range
start_mdy  = sp.start_date.strftime("%m-%d-%Y")           # for Julian-day conversion
end_year   = sp.end_date.year
iprint     = sp.iprint
sim_period = (sp.end_date - sp.start_date).days

print(f"Output start date : {start_str}")
print(f"Simulation length : {sim_period} days")
```

## 2  Pre-Processing Tab

The pre-processing steps configure the spatial linkage between SWAT and
MODFLOW.  The `swatmf` package handles all file-based I/O and spatial
operations (intersections, area calculations, link table generation) without
requiring QGIS.

- **Scenario C** (build from scratch) generates `mf_grid.gpkg` entirely in
  Python via `create_mf_grid`.
- **Scenarios A and B** (existing model) may still require QGIS to create the
  initial `mf_grid` shapefile if one does not already exist.

### 2.1  SWAT Inputs

Verify that the required SWAT output files are present in the working
directory before proceeding.

```{python}
required_swat = ["file.cio", "output.rch", "output.std"]
missing = [f for f in required_swat if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(wd, f))]

if missing:
    print("⚠ Missing SWAT files:", missing)
else:
    print("✔ All required SWAT files found.")
```

### 2.2  MODFLOW Options

Choose one of the three scenarios that matches your project:

| Scenario | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **A** | MODFLOW model files **and** grid shapefile are already available |
| **B** | MODFLOW model files are available but the grid shapefile is missing |
| **C** | No MODFLOW model yet — **build from scratch** (used in this example) |

**This workflow uses Scenario C** — the MODFLOW model is built from scratch
using `build_mf_model_from_dem` with the DEM from `data/swat/Source/dem.tif`.
Scenarios A and B are shown below as reference (not executed).

---

#### Scenario A — Existing QGIS plugin project *(reference — not executed)*

When the project folder was created by the QGIS plugin, `mf_grid.gpkg` and
all MODFLOW rasters are already in `GIS/org_shps/`.

```{python}
#| eval: false
import geopandas as gpd
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import parse_dis_file, grid_row_col

# Read MODFLOW grid dimensions from the .dis file.
dis = parse_dis_file(mf_wd)

print(f"Grid        : {dis.nrow} rows × {dis.ncol} cols  ({dis.n_cells:,} cells)")
print(f"Cell size   : delr={dis.delr} m  delc={dis.delc} m")
print(f"Transient   : {dis.transient}")
print(f"Top elevs   : min={min(dis.top_elevs):.2f}  max={max(dis.top_elevs):.2f} m")

# Build 1-based row/col index lists.
rows_all, cols_all = grid_row_col(dis)
print(f"First cell: row={rows_all[0]}, col={cols_all[0]}")

# mf_grid.gpkg is already in org_shps — just load it.
mfgrid_path = os.path.join(org_shps, "mf_grid.gpkg")
grid_gdf = gpd.read_file(mfgrid_path)
print(f"Grid cells loaded: {len(grid_gdf)}  "
      f"(rows={grid_gdf['row'].max()}, cols={grid_gdf['col'].max()})")
```

---

#### Scenario B — MODFLOW files present, grid shapefile missing *(reference — not executed)*

Parse the existing `.dis` file and create `mf_grid.gpkg` using the NW corner
of the model domain (from QGIS layer properties or the boundary shapefile):

```{python}
#| eval: false
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import parse_dis_file, create_mf_grid
import geopandas as gpd, glob

dis = parse_dis_file(mf_wd)

# Derive the NW corner from the model boundary shapefile.
bnd_gdf = gpd.read_file(os.path.join(org_shps, "mf_boundary.shp"))
b    = bnd_gdf.total_bounds
X_NW = b[0]   # left  (easting)
Y_NW = b[3]   # top   (northing)
print(f"NW corner: ({X_NW:.1f}, {Y_NW:.1f})")

# Create mf_grid.gpkg and save it to org_shps.
mfgrid_path = create_mf_grid(
    swatmf_folder = mf_wd,
    x_origin      = X_NW,
    y_origin      = Y_NW,
    crs           = 2193,          # EPSG code of your model CRS
    output_dir    = org_shps,
)
print(f"mf_grid.gpkg written to: {mfgrid_path}")
```

---

#### Scenario C — Build a new MODFLOW model from scratch *(active for this example)*

`build_mf_model_from_dem` generates all required MODFLOW input files **and**
`mf_grid.gpkg` in a single call.  The function:

* Dissolves the subbasin boundary and clips the DEM to it.
* Resamples the DEM to *cell_size* and derives the MODFLOW `ibound` mask.
* Builds the BAS, DIS, UPW, OC, NWT, and RCH packages using flopy.
* Writes `mf_grid.gpkg` with `grid_id`, `row`, `col`, `top_elev` columns.
* Saves MODFLOW parameter rasters (`top_elev.tif`, `bot_elev.tif`, `hk.tif`,
  `sy.tif`, `ss.tif`, `ih.tif`) to `org_shps` for visualisation in QGIS.

The MODFLOW files are written directly to `run_dir` so that SWAT and MODFLOW
files share one folder for the coupled simulation.

```{python}
import geopandas as gpd
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import build_mf_model_from_dem

# ── Dissolve subbasin polygons to get the watershed boundary ─────────────────
sub_gdf  = gpd.read_file(os.path.join(org_shps, "sub_org.shp"))
bnd_path = os.path.join(org_shps, "mf_boundary.shp")
sub_gdf.dissolve().to_file(bnd_path)
print(f"Watershed boundary written: {bnd_path}")

# ── MODFLOW model parameters ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
MF_NAME    = "qswatmod"   # base name for all MODFLOW files

# Cell size — 100 m gives a manageable grid for the example watershed
# (~16 km × 13 km → roughly 160 rows × 130 cols = ~20 000 cells).
CELL_SIZE  = 100.0        # [m]

# Aquifer parameters — adjust to match your site.
THICKNESS  = 50.0         # uniform aquifer thickness [m]
SY         = 0.2          # specific yield [-]
HK         = 5.0          # horizontal hydraulic conductivity [m/day]
SS         = 1e-4         # specific storage [1/m]
HEAD_DEPTH = 2.0          # initial head = DEM elevation − HEAD_DEPTH [m]

# CRS: None → inherit from the DEM (EPSG:2193 for this dataset).
CRS = None

# Simulation duration: SWAT run length + buffer.
duration = sim_period + 100
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

result_c = build_mf_model_from_dem(
    dem_path          = dem_path,       # data/swat/Source/dem.tif  (4 m, EPSG:2193)
    mf_folder         = run_dir,        # MODFLOW files written to the run folder
    mf_name           = MF_NAME,
    boundary_path     = bnd_path,       # dissolved watershed boundary
    cell_size         = CELL_SIZE,
    aquifer_thickness = THICKNESS,
    sy                = SY,
    head_depth        = HEAD_DEPTH,
    hk                = HK,
    ss                = SS,
    crs               = CRS,
    output_dir        = org_shps,       # mf_grid.gpkg + rasters → GIS/org_shps/
    sim_duration      = duration,
)

print(f"MODFLOW model '{MF_NAME}' written to : {run_dir}")
print(f"Grid dimensions : {result_c.nrow} rows × {result_c.ncol} cols "
      f"({result_c.nrow * result_c.ncol:,} cells)")
print(f"NW origin       : ({result_c.x_origin:.1f}, {result_c.y_origin:.1f})  [EPSG:2193 m]")
print(f"mf_grid.gpkg    : {result_c.grid_path}")

# Set mf_wd and mfgrid_path for the remainder of the workflow.
mf_wd       = run_dir
mfgrid_path = result_c.grid_path
```

```{python}
# Also copy mf_grid.gpkg into the nested GIS/org_shps under run_dir so the
# run folder mirrors the full QGIS plugin layout.
import shutil
_ = shutil.copy2(
    mfgrid_path,
    os.path.join(run_dir, "GIS", "org_shps", "mf_grid.gpkg")
)
print("mf_grid.gpkg mirrored into run_dir/GIS/org_shps/")
```

```{python}
# Inspect the resulting grid object.
import geopandas as gpd

grid_gdf = gpd.read_file(mfgrid_path)
print(f"Grid cells loaded : {len(grid_gdf)}")
print(f"  rows={grid_gdf['row'].max()}  cols={grid_gdf['col'].max()}")
print(f"  CRS: {grid_gdf.crs}")
print(f"  top_elev range: {grid_gdf['top_elev'].min():.1f} – "
      f"{grid_gdf['top_elev'].max():.1f} m")
```

If you need to add river cells after the initial build, derive them with
`compute_riv_params` / `write_riv_file` (see Section 2.4) and pass the
resulting DataFrame as the `riv_df` argument.

> **Manual alternative** — if you already have numpy elevation arrays (e.g.
> loaded from your own raster pipeline), you can call `create_mf_model` and
> `create_mf_grid` individually as shown in the collapsible block below.

<details>
<summary>Manual array approach (click to expand)</summary>

```{python}
#| eval: false
import numpy as np
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import create_mf_model, create_mf_grid

# Adjust NROW/NCOL/DELR/DELC to match your domain.
# For the qswatmod-test watershed (EPSG:2193, ~16 km × 13 km) at 100 m:
NROW, NCOL = 127, 156      # approximate — computed from DEM extents ÷ cell size
DELR = DELC = 100.0        # [m]

# NW corner of the grid in EPSG:2193 metres (from sub_org.shp total_bounds).
# X_NW = left extent; Y_NW = top extent.
X_ORIGIN = 1876887.0
Y_ORIGIN = 5773616.0

# Placeholder elevation arrays — replace with DEM-derived values in practice.
top_elev = np.full((NROW, NCOL), 300.0)
bot_elev = top_elev - 50.0   # 50 m thick aquifer

MF_MANUAL_FOLDER = os.path.join(out, "mf_manual")
os.makedirs(MF_MANUAL_FOLDER, exist_ok=True)

mf_manual = create_mf_model(
    mf_folder    = MF_MANUAL_FOLDER,
    mf_name      = "qswatmod_manual",
    top_elev     = top_elev,
    bot_elev     = bot_elev,
    delr         = DELR,
    delc         = DELC,
    hk           = 5.0,
    ss           = 1e-4,
    sy           = 0.2,
    initial_head = top_elev - 2.0,
    riv_df       = None,
    sim_duration = duration,
)

mfgrid_path_manual = create_mf_grid(
    swatmf_folder = MF_MANUAL_FOLDER,
    x_origin      = X_ORIGIN,
    y_origin      = Y_ORIGIN,
    crs           = 2193,           # EPSG:2193 — NZGD2000 / NZ Transverse Mercator
    output_dir    = org_shps,
)
print("mf_grid.gpkg written to:", mfgrid_path_manual)
```

</details>

After either build route, validate the MODFLOW inputs and generate the
required `modflow.mfn` helper file:

```{python}
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import check_modflow_files

# Validate the MODFLOW model folder (run_dir for this Scenario C example,
# or wherever mf_wd was set for Scenarios A/B).
check_result = check_modflow_files(mf_wd)
for msg in check_result["messages"]:
    print(msg)
print("Status:", check_result["status"])
```

`check_modflow_files` replicates the **Check MODFLOW file** button in the
QSWATMOD2 plugin.  It validates that the required `.dis`, `.nam`, and `.oc`
files exist, generates `modflow.mfn` (adjusting unit numbers so they do not
conflict with SWAT-MODFLOW), and updates the `HEAD SAVE UNIT` value in the
`.oc` file.

You can also run the two sub-steps individually:

```{python}
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import create_modflow_mfn, modify_modflow_oc

mfn_path = create_modflow_mfn(mf_wd)
print("modflow.mfn written to:", mfn_path)

oc_path = modify_modflow_oc(mf_wd)
print("OC file updated       :", oc_path)
```

> **This example (Scenario C)** — `mf_wd` is `run_dir`; the MODFLOW files
> were written there by `build_mf_model_from_dem` above.  For Scenarios A / B,
> ensure your pre-built MODFLOW files are present in `mf_wd` before this step.

### 2.3  Create the `modflow.obs` file

The `modflow.obs` file lists the MODFLOW grid cells that correspond to
groundwater-level observation wells.  Each row requires a `grid_id` (1-based
cell index = `(row - 1) × ncol + col`), `layer`, and `top_elev`.

> **Grid IDs vs well identifiers** — The correct grid IDs must be found by
> spatially joining the observation well point shapefile with `mf_grid.gpkg`.
> Well name columns in observed CSV files are identifiers, not MODFLOW cell IDs.
> The example below shows the workflow; substitute your own well point shapefile.

```{python}
# Read the MODFLOW grid dimensions — needed for post-processing and RT3D.
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import parse_dis_file
dis = parse_dis_file(mf_wd)
print(f"Grid: {dis.nrow} rows × {dis.ncol} cols  ({dis.n_cells:,} active cells)")
```

```{python}
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import create_modflow_obs, read_modflow_obs

# Spatial join: find which mf_grid cell each observation well falls in.
# Replace the path below with your own well point shapefile.
well_shp = os.path.join(org_shps, "obs_wells.shp")   # ← update filename

if os.path.isfile(well_shp):
    obs_pts  = gpd.read_file(well_shp)
    grid_gdf = gpd.read_file(mfgrid_path)

    if obs_pts.crs != grid_gdf.crs:
        obs_pts = obs_pts.to_crs(grid_gdf.crs)

    obs_joined = gpd.sjoin(
        obs_pts,
        grid_gdf[["grid_id", "top_elev", "geometry"]],
        how="left",
        predicate="within",
    )

    obs_valid = obs_joined.dropna(subset=["grid_id"]).copy()
    obs_valid["grid_id"] = obs_valid["grid_id"].astype(int)

    obs_wells = pd.DataFrame({
        "grid_id":  obs_valid["grid_id"].values,
        "layer":    1,
        "top_elev": obs_valid["top_elev"].values,
    })
    print("Observation wells assigned to grid cells:")
    print(obs_wells)

    # Write modflow.obs — mf_wd for the .dis lookup, table_dir for the output.
    obs_path = create_modflow_obs(mf_wd, obs_wells, output_dir=table_dir)
    print("modflow.obs written to:", obs_path)
else:
    # No well shapefile available — write a zero-record file.
    # Groundwater-level output will not be produced when modflow.obs is empty.
    obs_wells = pd.DataFrame(columns=["grid_id", "layer", "top_elev"])
    obs_path  = create_modflow_obs(mf_wd, obs_wells, output_dir=table_dir)
    print(f"⚠ No observation well shapefile found at:\n  {well_shp}")
    print(f"  Empty modflow.obs written to {obs_path}")
    print("  Update 'well_shp' above to enable groundwater-level output.")
```

### 2.4  River Connections

The river connection option determines which MODFLOW grid cells represent
river boundaries.  Choose one of the three options:

| Option | Description | MODFLOW layer name |
|--------|-------------|--------------------|
| **Option 1 — MODFLOW river only** | River cells taken directly from the `.riv` package | `mf_riv1` |
| **Option 2 — SWAT river only** | MODFLOW cells that spatially intersect the SWAT river network | `mf_riv2` |
| **Option 3 — Both networks** | Combination: Option 2 cells plus any Option 1 cells not already included | `mf_riv3` |

The cell selection and shapefile creation steps require QGIS.  Once the
river shapefile is ready, parse the hydraulic parameters and (if needed)
update the `.riv` package file:

```{python}
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import parse_riv_file, compute_riv_params, write_riv_file
import glob as _glob

# --- Option 1: read river cells directly from the existing .riv package ----
# Only applicable when a .riv file already exists in mf_wd.
riv_files = _glob.glob(os.path.join(mf_wd, "*.riv"))
if riv_files:
    riv_df = parse_riv_file(mf_wd)
    print(f"River cells found in .riv package: {len(riv_df)}")
    print(riv_df.head())
else:
    riv_df = None
    print("No .riv package found — use Option 2 or 3 to derive river cells "
          "from the SWAT river network (see below).")
```

```{python}
# --- Option 2 (active for Scenario C): intersect SWAT river network with grid
# The SWAT river shapefile (riv_org.shp) has Wid2 and Dep2 attributes.
# We spatially intersect it with the MODFLOW grid to get river_grid, then
# compute conductance and write the .riv file.

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import compute_riv_params, write_riv_file
from swatmf.preprocessing.linking import generate_river_grid
from swatmf.simulation import write_swatmf_river2grid

riv_org_path = os.path.join(org_shps, "riv_org.shp")
sub_org_path = os.path.join(org_shps, "sub_org.shp")

if os.path.isfile(riv_org_path) and os.path.isfile(mfgrid_path):
    # Step 1: intersect SWAT river lines with the MODFLOW grid and subbasins.
    # Returns: grid_id, subbasin, rgrid_len.
    # Also writes the river_grid link table to table_dir.
    river_grid_df = generate_river_grid(
        riv_path    = riv_org_path,
        mfgrid_path = mfgrid_path,
        sub_path    = sub_org_path,
        table_dir   = table_dir,    # writes river_grid to GIS/Table/
    )
    print(f"River–grid intersection: {len(river_grid_df)} cell-reach segments")

    # Step 2: join row, col, top_elev from mf_grid (needed by compute_riv_params).
    grid_gdf = gpd.read_file(mfgrid_path)[["grid_id", "row", "col", "top_elev"]]
    river_grid_df = river_grid_df.merge(grid_gdf, on="grid_id", how="left")

    # Step 3: join Wid2 and Dep2 from the SWAT river shapefile (per subbasin).
    riv_gdf = gpd.read_file(riv_org_path)[["Subbasin", "Wid2", "Dep2"]]
    riv_gdf = riv_gdf.rename(columns={"Subbasin": "subbasin"})
    # Aggregate to one row per subbasin (length-weighted mean would be ideal;
    # simple mean is used here as a reasonable approximation).
    riv_attrs = riv_gdf.groupby("subbasin")[["Wid2", "Dep2"]].mean().reset_index()
    river_grid_df = river_grid_df.merge(riv_attrs, on="subbasin", how="left")

    print(f"river_grid columns: {list(river_grid_df.columns)}")
    print(river_grid_df.head())

    # Step 4a: write swatmf_river2grid.txt — the file the Fortran executable reads
    # at runtime to map MODFLOW river cells back to SWAT subbasins.
    r2g_path = write_swatmf_river2grid(river_grid_df, run_dir)
    print(f"swatmf_river2grid.txt written: {r2g_path}  ({len(river_grid_df.groupby('grid_id'))} river cells)")

    # Step 4c: compute MODFLOW RIV package parameters and write the .riv file.
    riv_params = compute_riv_params(
        river_grid_df,
        riverbed_k     = 0.1,    # riverbed hydraulic conductivity [m/day]
        riverbed_thick = 0.5,    # riverbed thickness [m]
    )
    riv_path = write_riv_file(mf_wd, riv_params)
    print(f"RIV package written: {riv_path}  ({len(riv_params)} river cells)")
    riv_df = riv_params          # used in Section 7 (GW-SW exchange)
else:
    riv_df = None
    print("⚠ riv_org.shp or mf_grid.gpkg not found — skipping river connection.")
```

### 2.5  Linking Process

The linking process creates three tab-delimited ASCII tables read by the
SWAT-MODFLOW executable at runtime:

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `hru_dhru` | Maps each disaggregated HRU (dHRU) to its parent HRU and subbasin |
| `dhru_grid` | Maps each dHRU fragment to the MODFLOW grid cells it overlaps (sorted by grid × dHRU) |
| `grid_dhru` | Inverse mapping: sorted by dHRU × grid; header contains `nrow` and `ncol` |

All three files are generated using :mod:`swatmf.preprocessing.linking`, which
replicates the QGIS **Linking Process** panel using GeoPandas.

**Required input shapefiles** (created by the QGIS plugin):

| File | Contents | Location |
|------|----------|----------|
| `hru_org.shp` | Original SWAT HRU polygons | `GIS/org_shps/` |
| `sub_org.shp` | Original SWAT subbasin polygons | `GIS/org_shps/` |
| `mf_grid.gpkg` | MODFLOW grid polygons with `grid_id` | `GIS/org_shps/` |

The link tables (`hru_dhru`, `dhru_grid`, `river_grid`) are written to
`GIS/Table/`.  For this Scenario C example they are generated here; for a
project set up with the QGIS plugin they are already present.

```{python}
import geopandas as gpd
from swatmf.preprocessing.linking import generate_link_tables

# ── Input file paths (QGIS plugin layout) ───────────────────────────────────
hru_path    = os.path.join(org_shps, "hru_org.shp")
sub_path    = os.path.join(org_shps, "sub_org.shp")
# mfgrid_path was set in Section 2.2; default is org_shps/mf_grid.gpkg.
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

result = generate_link_tables(
    hru_path          = hru_path,
    sub_path          = sub_path,
    mfgrid_path       = mfgrid_path,
    table_dir         = table_dir,    # GIS/Table/ — same folder the plugin uses
    swatmf_folder     = mf_wd,        # reads .dis to embed nrow/ncol in grid_dhru
    # Optional: save intermediate GeoPackages for QA/QC in QGIS
    save_intermediate = True,
    intermediate_dir  = sm_shps,      # GIS/SMshps/
)

for name, fpath in result.items():
    status = "✔ found" if os.path.isfile(fpath) else "⚠ MISSING"
    print(f"  {name:<15} {status}  →  {fpath}")
```

Inspect the first few lines of each file:

```{python}
for name, fpath in result.items():
    print(f"\n--- {name} ---")
    with open(fpath) as fh:
        for i, line in enumerate(fh):
            if i >= 6:
                break
            print(line, end="")
```

If you need to run only one part of the pipeline (e.g. to inspect intermediate
results), the individual functions are also available:

```{python}
from swatmf.preprocessing.linking import (
    create_dhru,       # HRU multipart → singlepart dHRUs
    build_hru_dhru,    # dHRU × subbasin intersection
    export_hru_dhru,   # write hru_dhru file
    build_dhru_grid,   # dHRU × MODFLOW grid intersection
    export_dhru_grid,  # write dhru_grid file
    export_grid_dhru,  # write grid_dhru file (inverse sort, nrow/ncol header)
)

hru_gdf    = gpd.read_file(hru_path)       # SWAT HRU polygons (org_shps/hru_org.shp)
sub_gdf    = gpd.read_file(sub_path)       # SWAT subbasin polygons (org_shps/sub_org.shp)
mfgrid_gdf = gpd.read_file(mfgrid_path)   # MODFLOW grid polygons (org_shps/mf_grid.gpkg)

# Step-by-step pipeline
dhru          = create_dhru(hru_gdf)
hru_dhru_gdf  = build_hru_dhru(dhru, sub_gdf)
dhru_grid_gdf = build_dhru_grid(dhru, mfgrid_gdf)

print(f"dHRUs             : {len(dhru)}")
print(f"hru_dhru records  : {len(hru_dhru_gdf)}")
print(f"dhru_grid records : {len(dhru_grid_gdf)}")
```

### 2.6  Create Linkage Files

The SWAT-MODFLOW executable expects **all** inputs — SWAT files, MODFLOW
packages, link tables, and `modflow.mfn` — assembled in a single run
directory (`run_dir`).  Two copy steps bring everything together:

#### 2.6a  Copy link tables (HRU–MODFLOW mapping)

The link tables in `GIS/Table/` (created by the QGIS plugin or by
`generate_link_tables` in Section 2.5) are copied into `run_dir`:

```{python}
from swatmf.simulation import copy_link_files

link_copied = copy_link_files(
    table_dir     = table_dir,    # source: GIS/Table/
    swatmf_folder = run_dir,      # destination: SWAT-MODFLOW/ (run folder)
)

print(f"Link tables copied ({len(link_copied)} files):")
for f in link_copied:
    print(f"  {os.path.basename(f)}")
```

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `hru_dhru` | dHRU → HRU / subbasin mapping |
| `dhru_grid` | dHRU → MODFLOW grid mapping (sorted by grid × dHRU) |
| `grid_dhru` | dHRU → MODFLOW grid mapping (sorted by dHRU × grid) |
| `river_grid` | MODFLOW river-cell routing table |

#### 2.6b  Copy MODFLOW model files

The MODFLOW input packages (`.dis`, `.bas`, `.nam`, `.nwt`, `.upw`, `.riv`,
`.oc` …) and `modflow.obs` must be present in `run_dir` alongside the SWAT
files.  `copy_modflow_files` copies them from `mf_wd` and regenerates
`modflow.mfn` with correct bare-filename references.

For **Scenario C** the MODFLOW files were written directly into `run_dir` by
`build_mf_model_from_dem`, so `mf_wd == run_dir` and no copy is needed.
For **Scenarios A / B** `mf_wd` is a separate folder and the copy is required.

```{python}
from swatmf.simulation import copy_modflow_files
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import create_modflow_mfn
import os

if os.path.realpath(mf_wd) == os.path.realpath(run_dir):
    # Scenario C: MODFLOW files already in run_dir — nothing to copy.
    # Regenerate modflow.mfn here so any .riv written in Section 2.4 is
    # included (check_modflow_files in Section 2.3 ran before the .riv existed).
    print("MODFLOW files are already in run_dir — skipping copy.")
    create_modflow_mfn(run_dir)
    print("modflow.mfn regenerated (RIV injection applied if .riv present).")
else:
    # Scenarios A / B: copy from the separate MODFLOW model folder.
    # copy_modflow_files calls create_modflow_mfn internally.
    mf_copied = copy_modflow_files(
        mf_folder     = mf_wd,
        swatmf_folder = run_dir,
    )
    print(f"MODFLOW files copied ({len(mf_copied)} files):")
    for f in mf_copied:
        print(f"  {os.path.basename(f)}")
```

#### 2.6c  Copy the executable

The SWAT-MODFLOW executable from `SM_exes/` must also be present in `run_dir`:

```{python}
import shutil, glob

exe_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(exe_dir, "swatmf_rel*.exe")) + \
            glob.glob(os.path.join(exe_dir, "SWAT-MODFLOW*.exe"))

for exe in exe_files:
    dest = os.path.join(run_dir, os.path.basename(exe))
    _ = shutil.copy2(exe, dest)
    print(f"Copied: {os.path.basename(exe)}")
```

Verify that everything the executable needs is now in place:

### 2.7  RT3D — Reactive Transport Pre-Processing (optional)

If you plan to simulate nitrogen and phosphorus transport in the groundwater
system, create the RT3D input files here.  RT3D requires the MODFLOW model to
be already set up (grid dimensions are read from the `.dis` file).

The `swatmf.preprocessing.rt3d` module writes all six RT3D package files plus
the master `rt3d_filenames` list:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `.btn` | Basic Transport — species, porosity, ICBUND, initial concentrations, output times |
| `.dsp` | Dispersion — longitudinal dispersivity and transverse/vertical ratios |
| `.rct` | Reaction — denitrification kinetics (IREACT=10), sorption, bulk density |
| `.gcg` | Implicit GCG solver settings |
| `.adv` | Advection method selection |
| `.ssm` | Source/Sink Mixing (minimal — concentrations are passed at runtime via SMRT) |
| `rt3d_filenames` | Maps package codes to file paths for the executable |

```{python}
from swatmf.preprocessing.rt3d import RT3DConfig, write_rt3d_model
from swatmf.preprocessing.modflow import parse_dis_file

# ── Read grid dimensions from the existing MODFLOW .dis file ────────────────
import glob as _glob

dis_files = _glob.glob(os.path.join(mf_wd, "*.dis"))
if dis_files:
    dis_info = parse_dis_file(mf_wd)
    NROW = dis_info.nrow
    NCOL = dis_info.ncol
    print(f"Grid: {NROW} rows × {NCOL} cols (from {os.path.basename(dis_files[0])})")
else:
    # Fallback: use dimensions from the parsed dis object (Section 2.2).
    NROW = dis.nrow
    NCOL = dis.ncol
    print(f"Grid: {NROW} rows × {NCOL} cols (from Section 2.2 dis object)")
```

```{python}
# ── Configure RT3D parameters ───────────────────────────────────────────────
rt3d_cfg = RT3DConfig(
    model_name   = "rt3d_model",
    nrow         = NROW,
    ncol         = NCOL,
    nlay         = 1,

    # Transport properties
    porosity     = 0.30,       # scalar: applied to all active cells

    # Initial concentrations [mg/L]
    initial_conc_no3 = 0.5,    # uniform background NO₃
    initial_conc_p   = 0.01,   # uniform background P

    # Dispersion
    longitudinal_dispersivity = 10.0,   # [m]
    ratio_h_to_l              = 0.1,
    ratio_v_to_l              = 0.01,
    effective_molecular_diffusion = 0.0,

    # Reaction
    bulk_density       = 1.50,   # [g/cm³]
    sorption_no3       = 0.0,    # no sorption for NO₃
    sorption_p         = 0.0,    # no sorption for P
    k_denitrification  = 0.01,   # first-order rate [1/day]
    k_half_saturation  = 10.0,   # Monod half-saturation [mg/L]

    # Observation cells (optional) — use same cells as MODFLOW obs
    # obs_cells = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(wd, "modflow.obs"), ...)
)

# ── Write output times (e.g. daily for 1 year) ─────────────────────────────
# Adjust to match your simulation length
output_times = list(range(1, 366))
```

```{python}
# ── Write all RT3D files to the run directory ───────────────────────────────
rt3d_files = write_rt3d_model(run_dir, rt3d_cfg, output_times=output_times)

print("RT3D files written:")
for pkg, path in rt3d_files.items():
    print(f"  {pkg:<12} → {os.path.basename(path)}")
```

::: {.callout-note}
Remember to enable RT3D in the simulation flags (Section 3.1):
```python
cfg.rt3d_active = True
```
Without this flag, the SWAT-MODFLOW executable will ignore the RT3D input
files even if they exist.
:::

---

## 3  Simulation Tab

The simulation tab writes `swatmf_link.txt`, which controls all SWAT-MODFLOW
run-time options.

### 3.1  Configure the simulation flags

```{python}
from swatmf.simulation import SwatmfLinkConfig, write_swatmf_link, summarise_link_config

# Start from defaults (matches the template file shipped with QSWATMOD2)
cfg = SwatmfLinkConfig.defaults()

# ── Edit these flags to match your scenario ─────────────────────────────────

# Pumping Rate Dictated by MODFLOW
# Enable if MODFLOW pumping wells supply irrigation water to SWAT HRUs.
cfg.pumping_mf = False          # True → MODFLOW Pumping → SWAT Irrigation

# Pumping Rate Dictated by SWAT
# Enable if SWAT auto-irrigation triggers groundwater extraction in MODFLOW.
cfg.pumping_swat = False        # True → SWAT Auto-Irrigation → MODFLOW Pumping

# MODFLOW DRAIN Cells to SWAT Subbasin Channels
# Enable if MODFLOW DRAIN-cell fluxes should be routed to SWAT channels.
cfg.drain_cells = False         # True → MODFLOW DRN → SWAT subbasin channels

# Read observation cells from modflow.obs
# Automatically disabled when no observation wells were defined (avoids Fortran EOF crash)
cfg.read_mf_obs = len(obs_wells) > 0   # True → enables groundwater-level output

# Optional output flags
cfg.output_swat_dp       = True
cfg.output_mf_recharge   = True
cfg.output_channel_depth = True
cfg.output_river_stage   = True
cfg.output_gwsw_grid     = True
cfg.output_gwsw_sub      = True
cfg.output_print_avg     = True

# RT3D reactive transport (nitrogen & phosphorus in groundwater)
# Enable only if RT3D input files were created in Section 2.7
cfg.rt3d_active = False         # True → activate RT3D N/P transport

# Output frequency: write results every N days (1 = every day)
cfg.output_step = 1

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print(summarise_link_config(cfg))
```

### 3.2  Groundwater Delay

Groundwater delay (`GW_DELAY`) controls how many days deep percolation from
SWAT takes to reach the water table in MODFLOW.

```{python}
# ── Option A: single value applied to all HRUs ──────────────────────────────
cfg.gw_delay_per_hru = False
cfg.gw_delay         = 31.0    # [days]

# ── Option B: one value per HRU (from the gw_delay QGIS layer) ─────────────
# cfg.gw_delay_per_hru = True
# cfg.gw_delay_values  = [10, 14, 31, 45, ...]  # one entry per HRU, sorted by HRU_ID
```

### 3.3  Write `swatmf_link.txt`

```{python}
link_path = write_swatmf_link(run_dir, cfg, sim_period=sim_period)
print("swatmf_link.txt written to:", link_path)

# Show the first 20 lines to confirm
with open(link_path) as fh:
    for i, line in enumerate(fh):
        if i >= 20:
            break
        print(line, end="")
```

### 3.4  Read back and verify

```{python}
from swatmf.simulation import read_swatmf_link

cfg_check = read_swatmf_link(run_dir)
print(summarise_link_config(cfg_check))
```

### 3.5  Pre-flight Check

Confirm that every file the executable needs is present in `run_dir` before
launching.  Re-run any flagged steps if anything is missing or still sitting
only in `GIS/Table/`.

```{python}
# Files the Fortran executable actually reads at runtime.
# hru_dhru / dhru_grid / grid_dhru are human-readable QA tables — NOT read by
# the exe — so they are excluded here.
# modflow.obs is only read when cfg.read_mf_obs is True (observation wells).
required_always = [
    "swatmf_link.txt",       # coupling flags  (step 3.3)
    "swatmf_grid2dhru.txt",  # grid→DHRU map   (step 2.5)
    "swatmf_dhru2grid.txt",  # DHRU→grid map   (step 2.5)
    "swatmf_dhru2hru.txt",   # DHRU→HRU map    (step 2.5)
    "swatmf_river2grid.txt", # river→grid map  (step 2.4)
    "modflow.mfn",           # MODFLOW name file (step 2.2)
]

all_ok = True
for fname in required_always:
    present = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(run_dir, fname))
    status  = "✔ in run_dir" if present else "✘ MISSING"
    if not present:
        all_ok = False
    print(f"  {fname:<30} {status}")

# modflow.obs only required when observation wells are active
if cfg.read_mf_obs:
    present = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(run_dir, "modflow.obs"))
    status  = "✔ in run_dir" if present else "✘ MISSING (copy from GIS/Table/)"
    if not present:
        all_ok = False
    print(f"  {'modflow.obs':<30} {status}")
else:
    print(f"  {'modflow.obs':<30} — skipped (read_mf_obs = False)")

# Spot-check that SWAT and MODFLOW input files are present
n_hru = len([f for f in os.listdir(run_dir) if f.endswith(".hru")])
n_dis = len([f for f in os.listdir(run_dir) if f.endswith(".dis")])
print(f"\n  SWAT .hru files in run_dir : {n_hru}")
print(f"  MODFLOW .dis files in run_dir: {n_dis}")
if n_hru == 0 or n_dis == 0:
    all_ok = False

if all_ok:
    print("\n✔ All required files are in run_dir — ready to simulate.")
else:
    print("\n⚠ Some files are missing.  Check the steps flagged above.")
```

### 3.6  Run Simulation


Once `swatmf_link.txt`, link tables, SWAT files, MODFLOW files, and the
executable are all in `run_dir`, launch the simulation.  The function
searches `run_dir` for a recognised executable name and starts it with `cwd`
set to `run_dir` so all relative file paths resolve correctly.

`run_simulation_monitored` streams `swatmf_log` to the console as the
executable writes it (init messages appear immediately; a dot is printed
every 2 s during the time-stepping loop so you can see it is not hung).

```{python}
from swatmf.simulation import run_simulation_monitored, validate_simulation

# Runs synchronously with live log output.
# Raises RuntimeError on non-zero exit code with the full log tail + stderr.
try:
    proc = run_simulation_monitored(
        swatmf_folder = run_dir,
        # exe_name = "swatmf_rel230818.exe",  # uncomment to override auto-detection
        poll_interval = 2.0,               # seconds between log checks
    )
except RuntimeError as e:
    print("Simulation crashed:\n", e)
```

To run silently in the background (non-blocking) and check on it manually:

```{python}
# from swatmf.simulation import run_simulation
# proc = run_simulation(run_dir, wait=False)
# # … do other work …
# proc.wait()
# print("Done — return code:", proc.returncode)
```

### 3.7  Validate simulation outputs

After the run, call `validate_simulation` to check whether the model
completed and all expected output files are non-empty.  It reads
`swatmf_log`, cross-references the active `swatmf_link.txt` flags, and
reports the size of every expected output file.

```{python}
report = validate_simulation(run_dir, cfg=cfg)
```

The report tells you:

| Section | What it checks |
|---------|---------------|
| **[1] Run log** | Whether `swatmf_log` ends with the completion marker; shows the last 15 lines on failure |
| **[2] Required inputs** | `swatmf_link.txt`, `modflow.mfn`, `hru_dhru`, `dhru_grid`, `grid_dhru`, `modflow.obs` (if enabled) |
| **[3] Output files** | Each file expected from the active flags — `output.rch`, `swatmf_out_MF_obs`, recharge, GW-SW, etc. — with file size |

Files under 200 bytes are reported as **EMPTY** even if they exist — the
executable writes a one-line header before running any timesteps, so a
header-only file means the crash occurred during initialisation.

If the log stops at **"MODFLOW files have been read"** without advancing to
simulation, common causes are:

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|-------------|-----|
| Log ends at "MODFLOW files have been read" | Link-table mismatch — cell count in `grid_dhru` header doesn't match the `.dis` file | Re-run `generate_link_tables` and `copy_modflow_files` |
| Log ends at "Observation cell file needed" | `modflow.obs` missing from `wd` | Run `copy_modflow_files` again |
| `output.rch` empty, MODFLOW outputs non-empty | SWAT input files missing or corrupted | Check `file.cio` and SWAT `.sub`/`.rte` files |

---

## 4  Streamflow

Simulated stream discharge is read from `output.rch`.  Observed data should
be in a CSV file with a `date` column and one column per gauge, placed in
`run_dir` alongside `output.rch`.

Outputs are read from `run_dir` (the coupled run folder).

```{python}
import shutil, glob
from swatmf.outputs.streamflow import (
    get_streamflow, compute_statistics, plot_streamflow, export_streamflow
)

# ── User inputs — update to match your observed data ────────────────────────
SUBBASIN   = 1          # subbasin number matching the observed data gauge
TIMESCALE  = "Daily"    # 'Daily', 'Monthly', or 'Annual'

# Place your observed streamflow CSV in run_dir and set the filename/column:
OBD_FILE = "stf_day.obd.csv"   # filename only (looked up in run_dir)
OBD_COL  = None                 # column name in the CSV, or None to skip obs

# If the obs file lives elsewhere, copy it first:
# shutil.copy("/path/to/stf_day.obd.csv", os.path.join(run_dir, OBD_FILE))
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

stf_df = get_streamflow(
    swatmf_folder=run_dir,
    subbasin=SUBBASIN,
    start_date=start_str,
    iprint=iprint,
    timescale=TIMESCALE
)

stf_df.head()
```

### 4.1  Plot

```{python}
fig, ax = plot_streamflow(
    df       = stf_df,
    subbasin = SUBBASIN,
    # obd_col  = OBD_COL,
    timescale= TIMESCALE,
)
plt.show()
```

### 4.2  Performance metrics

```{python}
if OBD_COL is not None and OBD_COL in stf_df.columns:
    stf_stats = compute_statistics(stf_df, obd_col=OBD_COL)
    print(f"NSE   : {stf_stats['nse']:.4f}")
    print(f"R²    : {stf_stats['rsq']:.4f}")
    print(f"PBias : {stf_stats['pbias']:.4f} %")
    print(f"RMSE  : {stf_stats['rmse']:.4f} m³/s")
else:
    stf_stats = None
    print("No observed streamflow data loaded; skipping metrics.")
```

### 4.3  Export

```{python}
fpath = export_streamflow(
    df=stf_df,
    out_folder=out,
    subbasin=SUBBASIN,
    obd_col=OBD_COL or "",
    timescale=TIMESCALE,
    stats=stf_stats,
)
print("Exported to:", fpath)
```

## 5  Groundwater Levels

Simulated hydraulic heads are read from `swatmf_out_MF_obs` using the
observation cell list in `modflow.obs`.

> **Column names vs grid IDs** — CSV columns in observed depth-to-water files
> are well identifiers, not MODFLOW cell IDs.  Use the grid IDs returned by
> the spatial join in Section 2.3.

```{python}
from swatmf.outputs.groundwater import (
    read_mf_obs, get_groundwater, compute_statistics as gw_stats,
    plot_groundwater, export_groundwater
)

# ── User inputs — update to match your site ─────────────────────────────────
# GRID_ID: the MODFLOW grid cell ID for the well of interest.
# Leave as None to auto-select the first observation cell from modflow.obs.
# (Set to a specific int once you know which cell you want, e.g. GRID_ID = 42)
GRID_ID        = None     # ← None = auto-select; or set an int from modflow.obs
GW_TIMESCALE   = "Daily"
DEPTH_TO_WATER = True     # True → convert simulated head to depth-to-water

# Place your observed groundwater CSV in run_dir and set the filename/column:
GW_OBD_FILE = "dtw_day.obd.csv"
GW_OBD_COL  = None        # column name in the CSV, or None to skip obs
# shutil.copy("/path/to/dtw_day.obd.csv", os.path.join(run_dir, GW_OBD_FILE))
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

mf_obs_meta = read_mf_obs(run_dir)
gw_df     = None
gw_metrics = None

if len(mf_obs_meta) == 0:
    print("⚠  No observation wells defined (modflow.obs absent or empty).")
    print("   Add observation cells to modflow.obs to enable GW-level output.")
    print("   Sections 5.1–5.3 will be skipped.")
else:
    # Auto-select first obs cell when GRID_ID is not specified
    if GRID_ID is None:
        GRID_ID = int(mf_obs_meta.index[0])
        print(f"GRID_ID not set — auto-selected first obs cell: {GRID_ID}")
    if GRID_ID not in mf_obs_meta.index:
        print(f"⚠  GRID_ID={GRID_ID} is not in modflow.obs "
              f"(available: {mf_obs_meta.index.tolist()}). Skipping GW section.")
        mf_obs_meta = mf_obs_meta.iloc[0:0]   # force empty so blocks below skip
    else:
        print(f"Observation cells defined in modflow.obs: {mf_obs_meta.index.tolist()}")
```

```{python}
if len(mf_obs_meta) > 0 and GRID_ID is not None:
    gw_df = get_groundwater(
        swatmf_folder  = run_dir,
        grid_id        = GRID_ID,
        start_date     = start_str,
        timescale      = GW_TIMESCALE,
        depth_to_water = DEPTH_TO_WATER,
        obd_file       = GW_OBD_FILE if GW_OBD_COL is not None else None,
        obd_col        = GW_OBD_COL,
    )
    gw_df.head()
else:
    print("Skipped — no observation cells available.")
```

### 5.1  Plot

```{python}
if gw_df is not None:
    _gw_obd_col = GW_OBD_COL if (GW_OBD_COL and GW_OBD_COL in gw_df.columns) else None
    fig, ax = plot_groundwater(
        df=gw_df,
        grid_id=GRID_ID,
        obd_col=_gw_obd_col,
        timescale=GW_TIMESCALE,
        depth_to_water=DEPTH_TO_WATER,
    )
    plt.show()
else:
    print("Skipped — no GW data available.")
```

### 5.2  Performance metrics

```{python}
if gw_df is not None and GW_OBD_COL is not None and GW_OBD_COL in gw_df.columns:
    gw_metrics = gw_stats(gw_df, grid_id=GRID_ID, obd_col=GW_OBD_COL)
    print(f"NSE   : {gw_metrics['nse']:.4f}")
    print(f"R²    : {gw_metrics['rsq']:.4f}")
    print(f"PBIAS : {gw_metrics['pbias']:.4f} %")
    print(f"RMSE  : {gw_metrics['rmse']:.4f} m")
else:
    gw_metrics = None
    print("No observed groundwater data loaded; skipping metrics.")
```

### 5.3  Export

```{python}
if gw_df is not None:
    fpath = export_groundwater(
        df=gw_df,
        out_folder=out,
        grid_id=GRID_ID,
        obd_col=GW_OBD_COL or "",
        timescale=GW_TIMESCALE,
        stats=gw_metrics,
    )
    print("Exported to:", fpath)
else:
    print("Skipped — no GW data to export.")
```

## 6  MODFLOW Recharge

Gridded recharge values (one value per MODFLOW grid cell, per time step) are
read from `swatmf_out_MF_recharge*`.

> **Note:** The number of grid cells (`N_CELLS`) must be specified because
> the output file is written without an explicit row count.  You can obtain
> this from `dis.n_cells` (Section 2.2) or from the `mf_grid` shapefile.

```{python}
from swatmf.outputs.recharge import (
    read_recharge_dates, get_recharge,
    average_monthly_recharge,
    plot_recharge_timeseries, plot_avg_monthly_recharge
)

# ── User inputs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# N_CELLS must equal the number of active MODFLOW grid cells.
# Use dis.n_cells from Section 2.2 (Scenario A), or the row count of the
# active-cell mask from your BAS file.
N_CELLS       = dis.n_cells   # derived from the parsed .dis file above
RCH_TIMESCALE = "Monthly"     # 'Daily', 'Monthly', or 'Annual'
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

print(f"Active MODFLOW cells: {N_CELLS}")
rch_dates = read_recharge_dates(run_dir, timescale=RCH_TIMESCALE, start_date=start_mdy)
print(f"Available {RCH_TIMESCALE.lower()} recharge steps: {len(rch_dates)}")
print(f"  First: {rch_dates[0]}   Last: {rch_dates[-1]}")
```

```{python}
rch_df = get_recharge(
    swatmf_folder = run_dir,
    n_cells       = N_CELLS,
    start_date    = start_mdy,
    timescale     = RCH_TIMESCALE,
)

print(rch_df.shape)  # (n_dates, n_cells)
rch_df.iloc[:5, :5]
```

### 6.1  Spatial mean recharge over time

```{python}
fig, ax = plot_recharge_timeseries(rch_df)
plt.show()
```

### 6.2  Average monthly recharge

```{python}
if RCH_TIMESCALE == "Monthly":
    avg_rch = average_monthly_recharge(rch_df)
    fig, ax = plot_avg_monthly_recharge(avg_rch)
    plt.show()
```

---

## 7  Groundwater–Surface-Water Exchange

GW-SW exchange fluxes are read from `swatmf_out_MF_gwsw*`.  Positive values
indicate groundwater discharge to the stream; negative values indicate stream
losses to the aquifer.

> **Note:** GW-SW exchange coupling requires a `river_grid` table from GIS
> preprocessing (intersecting the stream network with the MODFLOW grid and
> subbasin polygons) to build `swatmf_river2grid.txt`.  Without it the output
> file contains 0 river cells per time step and `gwsw_df` will be empty.
> GW-SW output requires a non-empty `river_grid` table from Section 2.4.
> If no river cells were found, `gwsw_df` will be empty.

```{python}
from swatmf.outputs.gwsw import (
    read_gwsw_dates, get_gwsw,
    gwsw_basin_total,
    plot_gwsw_timeseries, export_gwsw
)

# ── User inputs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# get_gwsw() auto-detects the actual river-cell count from the output file,
# so any value of N_RIV_CELLS is safe (a warning is issued if it differs).
N_RIV_CELLS    = len(riv_df) if riv_df is not None else 0   # from Section 2.4
GWSW_TIMESCALE = "Daily"       # 'Daily', 'Monthly', or 'Annual'
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

gwsw_dates = read_gwsw_dates(run_dir, timescale=GWSW_TIMESCALE, start_date=start_mdy)
print(f"Available {GWSW_TIMESCALE.lower()} GW-SW steps: {len(gwsw_dates)}")
```

```{python}
gwsw_df = get_gwsw(
    swatmf_folder = run_dir,
    n_riv_cells   = N_RIV_CELLS,
    start_date    = start_mdy,
    timescale     = GWSW_TIMESCALE,
)

if gwsw_df.empty:
    print("No GW-SW data available (0 river cells in output).")
    print("Provide a 'river_grid' GIS table to enable GW-SW coupling.")
else:
    print(gwsw_df.shape)  # (n_dates, n_river_cells)
    display(gwsw_df.head())
```

### 7.1  Basin total GW-SW exchange

```{python}
if not gwsw_df.empty:
    fig, ax = plot_gwsw_timeseries(gwsw_df, timescale=GWSW_TIMESCALE)
else:
    print("Skipped — no GW-SW data.")
```

### 7.2  Export

```{python}
if not gwsw_df.empty:
    fpath = export_gwsw(gwsw_df, out, timescale=GWSW_TIMESCALE)
    print("Exported to:", fpath)
else:
    print("Skipped — no GW-SW data.")
```

## 9  RT3D — Reactive Transport Post-Processing

This section reads and visualises the RT3D concentration outputs produced by
the SWAT-MODFLOW-RT3D coupled model.  It is only relevant when
`cfg.rt3d_active = True` was set in Section 3.

### 9.1  Read concentration grids

```{python}
from swatmf.outputs.rt3d import read_rt3d_conc, plot_conc_map

# Read monthly NO₃ concentrations
try:
    no3_monthly = read_rt3d_conc(
        run_dir,
        species="no3",
        freq="monthly",
        start_date=sp.start_date_warmup.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
    )
    print(f"NO₃ monthly: {len(no3_monthly)} time steps loaded")
    # Show grid shape of first time step
    first_key = list(no3_monthly.keys())[0]
    print(f"  Grid shape: {no3_monthly[first_key].shape}")
except FileNotFoundError as e:
    no3_monthly = None
    print(f"⚠ {e}")
```

```{python}
# Read monthly P concentrations
try:
    p_monthly = read_rt3d_conc(
        run_dir,
        species="p",
        freq="monthly",
        start_date=sp.start_date_warmup.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
    )
    print(f"P monthly: {len(p_monthly)} time steps loaded")
except FileNotFoundError as e:
    p_monthly = None
    print(f"⚠ {e}")
```

### 9.2  Concentration maps

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

if no3_monthly:
    # Plot last available month
    last_key = list(no3_monthly.keys())[-1]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

    plot_conc_map(no3_monthly[last_key], title=f"NO₃ — {last_key}",
                  cmap="YlOrRd", ax=axes[0])

    if p_monthly:
        last_key_p = list(p_monthly.keys())[-1]
        plot_conc_map(p_monthly[last_key_p], title=f"P — {last_key_p}",
                      cmap="YlGnBu", ax=axes[1])

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
else:
    print("No RT3D concentration output available — skipping maps.")
```

### 9.3  GW–SW nutrient exchange

```{python}
from swatmf.outputs.rt3d import read_rt3d_rivflux, plot_rivflux_ts

try:
    no3_flux = read_rt3d_rivflux(
        run_dir, species="no3", by="subbasin",
        start_date=sp.start_date_warmup.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
    )
    ax = plot_rivflux_ts(no3_flux, species="NO₃")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    print(f"NO₃ GW-SW flux: {len(no3_flux)} time steps, "
          f"{no3_flux.shape[1]} subbasins")
except FileNotFoundError as e:
    no3_flux = None
    print(f"⚠ {e}")
```

```{python}
try:
    p_flux = read_rt3d_rivflux(
        run_dir, species="p", by="subbasin",
        start_date=sp.start_date_warmup.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
    )
    ax = plot_rivflux_ts(p_flux, species="P")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
except FileNotFoundError as e:
    p_flux = None
    print(f"⚠ {e}")
```

### 9.4  Recharge nutrient concentrations

```{python}
from swatmf.outputs.rt3d import read_rt3d_recharge_conc

try:
    rech_no3 = read_rt3d_recharge_conc(
        run_dir, species="no3", by="subbasin",
        start_date=sp.start_date_warmup.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
    )
    print(f"NO₃ recharge conc: {len(rech_no3)} time steps, "
          f"{rech_no3.shape[1]} subbasins")
    print(rech_no3.describe().round(4))
except FileNotFoundError as e:
    rech_no3 = None
    print(f"⚠ {e}")
```

## 10  Performance Metrics Summary

Aggregate all available metrics into a single summary table.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

records = []

if stf_stats is not None:
    records.append({
        "Variable": f"Streamflow (subbasin {SUBBASIN})",
        "Timescale": TIMESCALE,
        "NSE":   round(stf_stats["nse"],   4),
        "R²":    round(stf_stats["rsq"],   4),
        "PBIAS": round(stf_stats["pbias"], 4),
        "RMSE":  round(stf_stats["rmse"],  4),
    })

if locals().get("gw_metrics") is not None:
    records.append({
        "Variable": f"Groundwater Level (grid {locals().get('GRID_ID', '?')})",
        "Timescale": locals().get("GW_TIMESCALE", "Daily"),
        "NSE":   round(gw_metrics["nse"],   4),
        "R²":    round(gw_metrics["rsq"],   4),
        "PBIAS": round(gw_metrics["pbias"], 4),
        "RMSE":  round(gw_metrics["rmse"],  4),
    })

if records:
    summary = pd.DataFrame(records).set_index("Variable")
    display(summary)
else:
    print("No observed data was loaded; no statistics to summarise.")
```

## Appendix — Package structure

```
swatmf/
├── __init__.py              # exposes Paths, parse_file_cio
├── paths.py                 # Paths class (replaces dirs_and_paths)
├── sim_period.py            # parse_file_cio (replaces define_sim_period)
├── metrics.py               # nse, rmse, pbias, rsq, all_metrics
├── simulation.py            # SwatmfLinkConfig, write/read swatmf_link.txt
├── preprocessing/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── modflow.py           # parse_dis_file, create_mf_model, modflow.obs, etc.
│   ├── linking.py           # generate_link_tables (hru_dhru, dhru_grid)
│   └── rt3d.py             # RT3DConfig, write_rt3d_model (BTN/DSP/RCT/GCG/ADV/SSM)
└── outputs/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── streamflow.py        # post_i_sw.py  → get_streamflow, plot_streamflow
    ├── groundwater.py       # post_ii_gw.py → get_groundwater, plot_groundwater
    ├── recharge.py          # post_iii_rch.py → get_recharge, plot_recharge_*
    ├── gwsw.py              # post_iv_gwsw.py → get_gwsw, plot_gwsw_timeseries
    ├── water_balance.py     # post_v_wb.py → get_water_balance, plot_water_balance
    └── rt3d.py              # post_vii_nitrate.py → read_rt3d_conc, plot_conc_map
```

### Correspondence to QSWATMOD2 plugin tabs

| Workflow step | Plugin tab / module | `swatmf` module |
|---|---|---|
| Project paths | `QSWATMOD2.dirs_and_paths` | `swatmf.paths.Paths` |
| Simulation period | `QSWATMOD2.define_sim_period` | `swatmf.sim_period.parse_file_cio` |
| MODFLOW grid / model | **Pre-Processing** / `modflow_functions.py` | `swatmf.preprocessing.modflow` |
| Build MF model (flopy) | **Pre-Processing** / `writeMF.writeMFmodel` | `swatmf.preprocessing.modflow.create_mf_model` |
| modflow.obs | **Pre-Processing** / `modflow_functions.export_modflow_obs` | `swatmf.preprocessing.modflow.create_modflow_obs` |
| River connections | **Pre-Processing** / `modflow_functions.mf_riv*` | `swatmf.preprocessing.modflow.parse_riv_file` |
| RT3D input files | **Pre-Processing** / `write_rt3d.write_rt3d_inputs` | `swatmf.preprocessing.rt3d.write_rt3d_model` |
| swatmf_link.txt | **Simulation** / `runSim_link.create_swatmf_link` | `swatmf.simulation.write_swatmf_link` |
| Streamflow | **Post-Processing** / `post_i_sw.py` | `swatmf.outputs.streamflow` |
| Groundwater levels | **Post-Processing** / `post_ii_gw.py` | `swatmf.outputs.groundwater` |
| MODFLOW recharge | **Post-Processing** / `post_iii_rch.py` | `swatmf.outputs.recharge` |
| GW-SW exchange | **Post-Processing** / `post_iv_gwsw.py` | `swatmf.outputs.gwsw` |
| Water balance | **Post-Processing** / `post_v_wb.py` | `swatmf.outputs.water_balance` |
| RT3D concentrations | **Post-Processing** / `post_vii_nitrate.py` | `swatmf.outputs.rt3d` |
| Objective functions | `pyfolder/utils.py ObjFns` | `swatmf.metrics` |
